missed.fact: Reminder has TWO stamps, scheduleUpdatedAt and statusUpdatedAt, each encoded as Millis and Device columns. The stamp is a per-field-group merge stamp, not the row's identity. Identity is the ULID primary key `id`.
The JSON column names are scheduleUpdatedAtMillis / scheduleUpdatedAtDevice. There is no 'scheduleUpdatedByDevice' in the codec, so claim 1's field name is wrong as well.

A reminder's deletedAt is bundled into the schedule group. A delete therefore competes with due/repeat edits, not with done/notified flips, so a status-only change on B does not resurrect a row that A deleted. The status group can still carry done/notified onto the tombstone.

Both stamps are clamped to now at comparison time when they are more than 24h in the future. The clamped stamp is persisted as the winner's effective stamp, and it is still replaced by any genuinely later edit. A skewed clock therefore cannot win forever. A skewed clock of less than 24h ahead does win conflicts.

On a first-time arrival the incoming row is stored as sent, stamp included, with no clamp. A tombstone older than 90 days is stored by applyIncoming and then purged by the GC sweep in the same import transaction. A fresh device therefore keeps live rows and recent tombstones but loses old tombstones. The FK-safe purge can skip some rows, because it swallows SQLiteConstraintException.

A tombstone is purged when deletedAtMillis < now-90d, measured against deletedAt and not against the stamp. The local GC also runs after every import. A device that was offline for over 90 days and still holds the live row re-exports it, and every other device re-adopts it because it has no local copy (resurrection).

The 'own' file chronicle-sync-<thisDevice>.json is skipped on read. Peer files are skipped when lastModified has not moved since the last read. A lastModified of 0 forces a read every run. The folder sync reads first and writes second.
Tie-break is a string comparison of deviceId.value, so the lexicographically larger device id wins a same-millisecond tie. The persisted stamp is truncated to epoch millis.

Each entity (except Reminder) has only a single `updatedAt` stamp. A concurrent rename on A and a colour change on B therefore means one whole row overwrites the other. The field stamps are per field group, which for 10 of 11 entity types is the whole row. Only Reminder has 2 groups.

Sessions and entries also carry extra identity or cross-row data: Session.plannedRun is packed into one 'plannedRun' string. Entry packs one of four value kinds into the columns numberValue, boolValue, ratingValue and choiceId. A reminder's repeatIntervalMillis holds a bitmask for WEEKDAYS and a packed value for RANDOM_DAYS, so it carries a second meaning beyond interval millis.

The import is transactional and the merge happens per row inside db.withTransaction. A record that cannot be decoded is skipped and counted in `undecodable`. A schemaVersion other than CURRENT rejects the whole file.
